name: After § 5
title: REPORT on the situation of fundamental rights in the European Union in 2024 and 2025
part_text: 5a. Recognises the importance of safeguarding pluralism in democratic societies, including through the role of civil society organisations contributing to public debate on issues such as human dignity, the protection of life, family policies and social values; underlines that the free expression of differing ethical, philosophical or religious positions must be respected and protected, in accordance with the fundamental rights to freedom of thought, conscience, religion and association; highlights that such expressions should not be subject to stigmatisation, discrimination or undue restrictions;
